findings.claim: Each material guard event holds the head and voids the activation tuple. Quick Order then stays unavailable after any matching lot receipt, quality update, price or product edit, or alias insert until an owner re-activates it under separate authority. This replaces the prior advance-only epoch model, and it is not registered as an owner decision.
findings.evidence: DOC71_DELTA.md:290-295 say a material change 'increments epoch and holds the head' and that every such change 'requires a separately authorized new activation before saving can resume'. :278-281: activation needs separate owner authority plus external publication/census/install/qualification receipts. Matrix :666: lots INSERT, scoped NEW → M. Prior model: RECOVERY_5C_RESOLUTION:98@f1821b6 'Relevant INSERT/DELETE advance' (epoch only); DOC49_5C_CORRECTION:9-19@462cf79 makes liveness a criterion; 7b1e606 carry-forward 7 frames these as in-flight refusal sources. Register :159-169 has no entry. Safety is not reduced.
findings.fix: Either register 'held on every material change, manual re-activation' as an explicit Samuel decision in the existing register, or decouple the two. In the decoupled form, the guard advances writer_epoch only. Activation binds a separate, strictly increasing activation generation (a head column plus the immutable tuple), and held→active requires a larger generation. The reader checks the tuple against active_revision_id and the generation, and intake keeps the preflight/post-head writer_epoch equality. The HI-3 defence is unchanged.

findings.claim: The guard never refuses writer transactions outside READ COMMITTED. Under REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE, its scope reads use the transaction snapshot, so an in-scope change can be classified OUT and bypass the gate and head (a guard-level fail-open).
findings.evidence: json guard.scopeRaceProposal relies on 'guards VOLATILE READ_COMMITTED fresh query'; DOC71_DELTA.md:575-577 claims 'new DML sees the new committed scope'. Only the commit and reader refuse other isolation levels (:241-243, :464). Hand-sim (reasoned, NOT RUN): W begins REPEATABLE READ with snapshot t0 (last_published X). Publish Y and activate Y pass SHARE NOWAIT because W holds no ROW EXCLUSIVE yet. Intake I preflights at (Y,E). W inserts a row in Y's scope but not X's; the guard reads at t0, classifies it OUT, takes no gate, and W commits inside I's post-head window. No non-test S writer uses RR/SERIALIZABLE on IN relations, so the gap is latent.
findings.fix: Before any classification, the guard raises 55000 unless current_setting('transaction_isolation')='read committed' (existing pattern: intake.sql:341, 20261001085559:209). Add an RR/SERIALIZABLE negative control.

findings.claim: The legal-binding INSERT rule bypasses alias-free rows. An alias-free row whose customer_ref is already another row's alias makes that identity ambiguous, yet it takes no gate, so it can commit inside an in-flight intake's post-head window.
findings.evidence: Matrix DOC71_DELTA.md:670 and the json legal INSERT row: 'empty or alias-free rows bypass'. The canonical writer checks only customer_ref equality before INSERT (20260809130000_research_early_access_hardening.sql:259-275@25858ad). The row CHECK only forbids customer_ref in its own alias_refs (:45-48). The lookup matches customer_ref=ref OR ref=ANY(alias_refs) and raises 21000 when it finds more than one (:280-298). An intake that resolved R via M1 holds FOR SHARE on M1, which does not block inserting customer_ref=R. Doc51 item 1 (7b1e606 carry-forward:11) keeps alias-bearing inserts IN for exactly this reason. NOT RUN.
findings.fix: Treat the INSERT as material if cardinality(NEW.alias_refs)>0 OR NEW.customer_ref = ANY(alias_refs) of any other existing row (evaluated as O after the statement). Add positive and negative controls.

findings.claim: The Markdown trust boundary names only a malicious superuser. In fact any session acting as O can forge activation with two DML statements.

findings.claim: The C-14 cost and blast radius are incomplete. The design implies runtime integrity on every guarded statement, including bypass paths, so any seal drift blocks writes to all 12 core platform relations.
findings.evidence: Every I/U/D matrix row lists an integrity refusal (DOC71_DELTA.md:658-671; json expectedRefusal), and :558-561 implies integrity runs on bypass paths. At S, integrity recomputes the full schema fingerprint (currentness.sql:422-424 and 45-83@25858ad). The cost model at :632-641 omits this. With ALWAYS guards, a seal drift, a missing head or an unexpected column (:647-649) refuses all writes to the 12 relations, including quantity-only reservation updates on lots and existing catalog, quality and Early Access writers. For example, installing the conditional price-tier candidate (20260905) would block price writes.
findings.fix: State whether integrity and the fingerprint run on bypass paths. If so, bound their cost, or use a cheap per-statement check (seal comment plus trigger states) and run the full fingerprint only on material paths. Register the blast radius on platform writers as an owner and qualification item.

findings.claim: Integrity does not cover several ways a statement-level guard can be bypassed silently: inheritance or partition children, rewrite rules and logical-replication apply.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from documented PostgreSQL behaviour, NOT RUN. Statement-level triggers fire for the explicitly named table, not for children or partitions targeted directly. Logical-replication apply fires row triggers only, not statement triggers. A DO INSTEAD rule rewrites the statement. The delta pins columns (DOC71_DELTA.md:647-649) but not relkind, pg_inherits, pg_rewrite or subscription membership for the 12 relations, and the S fingerprint covers rules only on owned relations (currentness.sql:77-78). Each bypass needs owner-level DDL.
findings.fix: Add to precheck, reapply, postcheck and runtime integrity, for each of the 12 relations: relkind='r', no pg_inherits rows in either direction, no rules, and not a subscription target.

findings.claim: An empty search_path does not stop unqualified type names resolving from pg_temp first. This matters because the definer guard runs in every writer's session.
findings.evidence: Documented search_path rule (NOT RUN): when pg_temp is not listed, it is searched first for relation and type names, never for functions or operators. The guard is SECURITY DEFINER with search_path '' (DOC71_DELTA.md:542-544) and fires in arbitrary writer sessions. :527-533 qualifies builtin calls but not type names or casts. Exploiting this needs a session with SQL and TEMP rights that writes an IN relation, which is owner-level in practice. S definer RPCs use the same pattern (intake.sql:141).
findings.fix: Schema-qualify every type name and cast in the guard body (pg_catalog.uuid, pg_catalog.jsonb and so on), keeping the pinned empty proconfig. Add this to the body-review checklist.

findings.claim: Builder condition 2 is broader than the quality-document writer. The existing lot identity trigger takes blocking shared readiness locks that can deadlock with a guard waiting for the gate.
findings.evidence: json WRITER_ORDER names only the quality-document writer; DOC71_DELTA.md:522-525 cites reservation-commands:239-283 (try-locks). The lots BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE OF identity trigger takes blocking pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared on product and variant readiness keys (20260727160000_research_inventory_reservation_commands.sql:293-329@25858ad). Hand-sim (NOT RUN): T1's earlier material statement holds the gate and head. T2's variant UPDATE takes the readiness try-lock, then its guard waits for the gate. T1's later lot INSERT waits on T2's key. The deadlock detector aborts one: fail-closed, but a liveness cost.
findings.fix: Bring every blocking lock reachable from existing row triggers on the 12 relations into the transaction-wide writer table. Apply the same pre-acquisition or no-wait rule before any guard drafting.

LENS T2 is mostly accurate, and every anchor I re-derived checks out. That covers:

- the RHQC key arithmetic and the two-int collision census;
- the lock.c waitMask reasoning;

  - The proconfig lock_timeout option was rejected without reason.
